title: Philadelphia clubs compared with New York and Atlantic City
summary: McRae says Philadelphia had a few hotels and clubs but no real excitement, unlike New York or Atlantic City.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Teddy, I get the feeling that Atlantic City had much more going for it musically than, say, Philadelphia, before the Depression (inaudible).
Well, Philadelphia never had -- Philadelphia had a few clubs and a few hotels, like the Bellevue-Stratford. They had some bands in there.
Philadelphia wasn't a -- up in North Philly, they had a few clubs. But Philadelphia wasn't a place, like, a big excitement place.
South Philly had -- that was an Italian neighborhood -- had the private big clubs.

And around the middle of uptown -- around like Market Street, Chestnut Street, Walnut Street (inaudible) around in Philly there, they had the average club like you had here. You know, like on the east side. You know, a few clubs.
But nothing sensational like New York
